mission: Ongoing original and copyright-respecting competitive research for Bizarre Past, What If in 40 Seconds and Little Wild Adventures. Grow views, engaged views, retention, subscribers and monetization eligibility through stronger content; never replicate third-party scripts/scenes/characters/music.
cadence: Weekly cross-channel research plus micro-research in each channel agent before preparing videos.
confidenceGuidelines: Use dated primary channel videos where possible; label third-party counts as dated estimates.
Compare views at similar video ages and by format; don't confuse correlation with causation.
Separate what we observed from what we propose to test. Never guarantee virality.
Use public watch pages and sources without unnecessary paid vidIQ calls; never buy credits automatically.
Use YT Analytics / Metricool for our channel performance, where available.
Made-for-kids videos often disable comments; do not interact with children's content to game engagement.

bizarre.name: History Matters
bizarre.observed: October 16 2026 historical question explainer runs 9:07 with more than 800k recorded views on a November 2 third-party snapshot. Repeated concise WHY-based historical titles and simplified animation.
bizarre.test: Open with spoken+on-screen Did you know; use a surprising, evidenced historical why-question and promise an answer; build to a concise revelation.
bizarre.confidence: High that packaging pattern exists; no direct causal proof for views.

bizarre.name: Squire Explains
bizarre.observed: Third-party similarity listing (Nov 2026) describes short animated strange-historical-why answers and an emerging audience.
bizarre.test: Look for undercovered bizarre historical incidents and simple but high-energy storytelling; verify actual channel videos before drawing performance conclusions.
bizarre.confidence: Candidate to check; video-level claims not yet verified.

whatif.name: QuirkScience
whatif.observed: Public film list mixes short, one-question science videos with source-backed 8–11 minute explorations; ocean, deep sea and space curiosities recur.
whatif.test: Test bright visually spectacular nature questions with one memorable scientific reveal; use original 35–40 sec Shorts and separate richer 8–10 min Sunday films.
whatif.confidence: Direct publisher portfolio, not a view-performance comparison.

whatif.name: xkcd’s What If?
whatif.observed: Absurd hypothetical questions explored with science and animation; different tone and scale from our positive Shorts.
whatif.test: Preserve the creative what-if question structure, but keep our optimistic tone and a payoff inside 40 seconds.

wild.name: Peep and the Big Wide World
wild.observed: Official preschool animation has consistent animal friends, small adventures and accessible science; activity curriculum covers movement, sound, water, plants, colour and patterns.
wild.test: Make Milo, the brown meerkat and BLUE bird solve one playful daily-life problem through active full-motion scenes and reveal the learning point together.
wild.confidence: Series structure and curriculum documented, but no video-level retention or virality claims.

wild.name: Numberblocks
wild.observed: Recurring number-characters and short stories introduce concepts through music and clear visual repetition.
wild.test: Use short original child-friendly counting/colour/song beats only where story and character continuity remain strong.

currentActionableHypotheses.nextTrial: First new Bizarre Past Short after 8 Nov

currentActionableHypotheses.measure: engaged views and retention at 24h/7d against channel's same-format baseline

currentActionableHypotheses.measure: Video-level watch time, child-friendly replays where data available, quality audit

currentActionableHypotheses.nextTrial: Next original Little Wild Short after quality gate

scope: Public channel portfolios and recent individual historical upload examples
lastResearch.limitations: No verified matched-age competitor video-level retention data, CTR or subscriber conversion; do not present as proof of why their channels succeeded.

requirements: 3 to 6 verified niche-matched channel or video examples total, rotating across our channels
Record source link, observation date, upload date, format/duration and views as available
Identify hook in first 2 seconds only if actually watched, not based on title
Summarize narrative pattern, visual pacing and concrete learning point
Provide 1-2 non-copying tests per owned channel, rank using evidence/effort/credit cost
After publishing compare own channel metrics at 24h/7d/28d
Update this JSON and production-control.json only with durable decisions; link to HQ and feed Telegram weekly summary
